items.title: Bound password guessing by account and contextual risk
items.objective: Determine whether repeated login failures are constrained across account, source, device, and time without enabling permanent victim lockout.
prerequisites: Owner-documented abuse model, expected limits, and explicit safe request/message ceiling
Disposable identities, synthetic resources/destinations, monitoring, and recovery/cleanup plan
steps: Establish one normal request and authoritative effect/cost control
Send a tiny sequential sample below the agreed ceiling, changing only one identity/source/resource dimension
Observe response, challenge/delay/rejection, account/resource state, provider side effects, alerts, and logs
Stop at the first control or anomaly and assess practical abuse from measured limits plus entropy/cost/business context

examples.note: Never brute-force, flood, spray, spam, exhaust storage, consume inventory, or create provider charges. Use only a tiny owner-approved sample.

items.manipulate: Request/message rate, identity/source distribution, recipient/resource fan-out, or one cost dimension within the written ceiling
items.secure_behavior: Layered per-account, per-resource, per-destination, contextual, and global controls make abuse uneconomic while avoiding permanent victim denial and preserving secure recovery.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a tiny approved sequence shows no meaningful account/context control and supports a practical guessing model
items.validation: Do not extrapolate from a handful of accepted requests alone; combine measured limits, entropy, lifetime, cost, business value, distributed model, alerts, and owner production configuration.
false_positives: adaptive controls can activate above the safe test ceiling
